title: They followed a homeless Rabbi…
paragraphs:
They followed a homeless Rabbi…
but somehow, the mission never lacked.

Food appeared.
Travel happened.
Needs were met.
So who was really financing Jesus?
Here’s the part many people skip.
It wasn’t kings. Not Rome. Not the temple system.
It was… transformed lives.
📖 Luke 8:2–3 opens the curtain:
“Joanna… Susanna, and many others were contributing to their support out of their own means.”
Let that sink in.
Women—healed, restored, set free—became partners in the mission.
The Hidden Treasury

Among them was Joanna, connected to Herod’s household.
Influence.

There was Mary Magdalene, once bound by demons.
Deliverance.

There were “many others.”
Unnamed. Unseen. But not unnoticed by heaven.
They gave from their own resources.

Not leftovers.
Not obligation.
Gratitude turned into generosity.
And there’s more…
Jesus also had a money bag, carried by Judas Iscariot (John 12:6).
Which means:

There was structure.
There was stewardship.
There was giving happening regularly.
Even if one of the carriers had a broken heart.
But here’s what we miss…
Jesus never begged.
He never manipulated.
He never built His mission on pressure.
He built it on transformation.

People who encountered grace
couldn’t help but support the mission of grace.
The deeper truth

God financed His Son’s ministry
through people whose lives were changed by that same Son.

Not obligation.
Overflow.
And that still hasn’t changed.

The Gospel moves forward today
on the backs of people who remember
who they used to be…
and who Jesus made them now.

So the real question isn’t just:
“Who financed Jesus?”
It’s this:
Has His grace moved you enough to become part of the mission?
Someone needs to hear this.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
